hypotheses.reconstruction_rule: G0001 = (F(x)-F(y))/(x-y); G0002 = F'(x), where df(x) is identified as the derivative of f at x under the stated assumption.
hypotheses.scientific_rationale: The raw Piecewise selects the generic divided-difference branch off the diagonal and a diagonal value on x=y. This is structurally a divided-difference family: the generic member is the first divided difference of f, and the diagonal member is its confluent derivative value.

hypotheses.reconstruction_rule: G0001 = F(x,y) for x≠y; G0002 = lim_{y->x} F(x,y), represented by df(x) in the raw Piecewise diagonal branch.
required_assumptions: The limit lim_{y->x} (f(x)-f(y))/(x-y) exists and is represented by df(x)
hypotheses.scientific_rationale: The expression is a local-confluence artifact: the same two-point quotient is used off the diagonal, while the diagonal value is supplied by the raw Piecewise as df(x). This hypothesis models the diagonal member as the confluent limit of the generic two-point quotient.
